title: Medical PDF Question Bank
description: Questions and answers based on the uploaded 56-page medical/community-health document. This is a study dataset, not medical advice.

questions.question: What is a village health worker?
questions.answer: A person who helps guide family members and neighbors toward better health and supports the well-being of the community.

questions.question: What is the first responsibility of a health worker?
questions.answer: To share health knowledge and teach people how to prevent and manage common health problems.

questions.question: Why is compassion important in health work?
questions.answer: People should be treated with kindness, dignity, and respect; emotional support can be very important to sick people and their families.

questions.question: How should a health worker respond to harmful traditional practices?
questions.answer: Address them carefully and respectfully, explaining why a safer approach may be better rather than simply telling people they are wrong.

questions.question: Why must a health worker know their limits?
questions.answer: They should do only what they have learned and can perform safely, avoiding procedures for which they are not properly trained.

questions.question: Why should health workers continue learning?
questions.answer: Ongoing study and learning from experts help them improve their skills and provide useful, up-to-date guidance.

questions.question: Why should health workers practice what they teach?
questions.answer: People often learn more from actions than words, so health workers should set a good example.

questions.question: What is the difference between felt needs and real needs?
questions.answer: Felt needs are problems people believe are important; real needs are the steps actually required to solve the problem in a lasting way.

questions.question: What four factors should be considered before starting a community project?
questions.answer: Felt needs, real needs, people's willingness to act, and available resources such as people, skills, materials, and money.

questions.question: What community conditions should be assessed when studying health needs?
questions.answer: Housing, sanitation, education, population, nutrition, water safety, food protection, health services, and common illnesses and injuries.

questions.question: Why are local resources useful for community health projects?
questions.answer: They are often more affordable, dependable, sustainable, and appropriate for local needs.

questions.question: Why should communities start new ideas with small experiments?
questions.answer: Small experiments reduce risk and help people learn from successes and failures before expanding an approach.

questions.question: How can poor sanitation contribute to diarrhea?
questions.answer: Poor sanitation and hygiene can help infections spread; clean practices and suitable latrines can reduce the risk.

questions.question: Why is malnutrition relevant to deaths from diarrhea in children?
questions.answer: Poorly nourished children may be less able to fight infection, so preventing malnutrition is also important.

questions.question: How does the book describe health beyond the absence of disease?
questions.answer: Health includes physical, mental, and social well-being.

questions.question: Why should treatment and prevention be balanced?
questions.answer: People need relief from current illness while also learning how to prevent future illness; both approaches support each other.

questions.question: Why can unnecessary medicine use be harmful?
questions.answer: It can waste money, cause side effects, encourage dependence, and contribute to antibiotic resistance.

questions.question: Do antibiotics treat common colds caused by viruses?
questions.answer: No. Antibiotics do not work against viral illnesses such as common colds and flu.

questions.question: What does the text identify as an important part of care for childhood diarrhea?
questions.answer: Providing enough fluids and continuing to feed the child; serious or persistent symptoms require medical assessment.

questions.question: Why is antibiotic resistance a concern?
questions.answer: Frequent or inappropriate antibiotic use can make bacteria harder to treat, reducing the effectiveness of important medicines.

questions.question: What is the difference between infectious and non-infectious diseases?
questions.answer: Infectious diseases are caused by organisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites and can spread; non-infectious diseases do not spread from person to person.

questions.question: Name four types of organisms that can cause infectious diseases.
questions.answer: Bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites.

questions.question: Do antibiotics work against most viral infections?
questions.answer: No. Antibiotics do not work against most viruses.

questions.question: How can fungal infections such as ringworm spread?
questions.answer: They can spread through contact with infected skin or clothing.

questions.question: How can malaria parasites spread to people?
questions.answer: Through mosquito bites.

questions.question: Why can similar symptoms require different diagnoses?
questions.answer: Different diseases can look alike but have different causes and require different treatments; examination and sometimes tests are needed.

questions.question: What is the difference between a symptom and a sign?
questions.answer: A symptom is what the person feels and reports; a sign is something observed during examination.

questions.question: What questions should be asked about a person's main health problem?
questions.answer: Ask what is troubling them, what makes it better or worse, when it began, whether it happened before, and whether others nearby have similar problems.

questions.question: What can pale lips or eyelids suggest according to the text?
questions.answer: They may suggest anemia.

questions.question: What can yellow skin and eyes suggest?
questions.answer: They suggest jaundice, which may be related to liver or gallbladder disease, among other causes.

questions.question: Why should breathing be observed carefully?
questions.answer: Breathing rate, depth, sounds, and difficulty can provide clues about illness and how serious it may be.

questions.question: What is the usual resting pulse range stated for adults in the book?
questions.answer: The book states 60 to 80 beats per minute for adults at rest.

questions.question: What may a weak and rapid pulse indicate?
questions.answer: It may indicate shock.

questions.question: Why should objects never be inserted into the ear?
questions.answer: Sticks, wires, and other hard objects can injure the ear.

questions.question: What may a very hard abdomen indicate?
questions.answer: It may indicate a serious condition such as appendicitis or peritonitis and needs urgent medical assessment.

questions.question: What may sudden facial weakness indicate?
questions.answer: It may be associated with head injury, stroke, or Bell's palsy; urgent medical assessment may be needed.

questions.question: Why should a very weak person who cannot move be repositioned?
questions.answer: Changing position several times a day helps prevent bed sores and may help reduce the risk of pneumonia.

questions.question: What should be monitored in a seriously ill person?
questions.answer: Changes in condition, vital signs, fluid intake, urination, and bowel movements should be recorded and shared with health workers.

questions.question: Name some danger signs that require immediate medical help.
questions.answer: Examples include severe breathing difficulty, unconsciousness, heavy bleeding, blue lips or nails, severe continuous abdominal pain, or repeated convulsions with fever.

questions.question: What should a caregiver do if a sick person can drink only small amounts?
questions.answer: Offer small sips frequently and monitor fluid intake; seek medical help when danger signs or severe dehydration are present.

questions.question: Why is cleanliness important when caring for a sick person?
questions.answer: Clean skin, clothes, sheets, and bedding help maintain comfort and reduce contamination risks.

questions.question: What does a sunken soft spot on a baby’s head indicate in the text?
questions.answer: It may be a sign of dehydration, which requires prompt attention and appropriate fluids or medical care.

questions.question: What might a bulging soft spot on a baby’s head indicate?
questions.answer: The text identifies it as a possible sign of meningitis, a serious condition requiring immediate medical help.

questions.question: Why is breastfeeding described as beneficial?
questions.answer: The text says breast milk provides nutrition and protection against infection.

questions.question: What is one warning about home remedies?
questions.answer: A remedy is not necessarily safe or effective simply because many people use it; some remedies can be harmful or delay proper care.

questions.question: Why are remedies involving human or animal waste dangerous?
questions.answer: They can cause serious infections, including tetanus, and should not be used.

questions.question: What does the text say about serious illnesses and home remedies?
questions.answer: Serious conditions such as pneumonia, tetanus, typhoid, tuberculosis, appendicitis, and fever after childbirth require prompt modern medical care.

questions.question: How can fear and belief affect health according to the text?
questions.answer: Strong fear or belief can affect stress and physical symptoms, while reassurance and understanding may help reduce fear.

questions.question: Why should a poisonous snakebite not be treated only with traditional remedies?
questions.answer: Traditional remedies cannot replace proper medical treatment; poisonous snakebites usually require antivenom and urgent medical care.

questions.question: What is the purpose of oral rehydration solution (ORS) in the text?
questions.answer: It is described as a way to help replace fluids when dehydration is a concern.

questions.question: What are some possible causes of malnutrition mentioned in the book?
questions.answer: Lack of knowledge about feeding, insufficient land or income, unfair resource distribution, poor farming practices, large family size, misuse of money, and lack of planning.

questions.question: Why should a community examine food production and land use?
questions.answer: Food production and land use affect whether families have enough food now and in the future.

questions.question: What is one way communities can improve food security?
questions.answer: Examples include family gardens, improved farming methods, crop rotation, irrigation, fish farming, composting, and better crop storage.

questions.question: Why is fair distribution of resources discussed as a health issue?
questions.answer: Access to land, food, and wealth can affect nutrition, family security, and overall health.

questions.question: How should a health worker treat people regardless of income?
questions.answer: They should treat everyone with dignity and should not refuse care to someone because they are poor.

questions.question: Why should community health workers understand local beliefs?
questions.answer: Respecting beliefs helps build trust and makes it easier to discuss safer health practices and encourage change.

questions.question: What should be done when symptoms are serious or unclear?
questions.answer: Seek help from a trained health worker or doctor; special tests may be needed.

questions.question: Why is recording findings useful during examination?
questions.answer: Records help communicate observations to another health worker and support assessment of the person's condition.

questions.question: What can rapid or difficult breathing suggest?
questions.answer: It may indicate a lung illness or another serious problem and should be assessed in context, especially if breathing is severely difficult.

questions.question: What is one way to help prevent constipation described in the book?
questions.answer: Drink enough water and eat fiber-rich foods such as whole grains, fruits, and vegetables.

questions.question: Why should enemas and laxatives be used cautiously?
questions.answer: The text warns they can cause harm in some conditions, including severe abdominal pain, dehydration, and illness in young children.

questions.question: What is the book's overall message about community health?
questions.answer: Improving health requires education, compassion, prevention, appropriate treatment, local cooperation, and attention to social and economic causes.
